title: Geo-Anchor Policy Engine and Retention Evidence Stream for Hosted Endpoints
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: Customers operating under data residency obligations frequently ask for deterministic controls on where hosted inference runs and for machine-verifiable evidence bundles proving residency and retention policy enforcement. This ticket scopes an engine that lets tenants declare geo-anchor policies for hosted API endpoints, map retention profiles to routes, and produce an automated, tamper-evident evidence stream for audit requests.

Goals: 1) Provide a policy DSL and Console UX to express: strict pin (hard region), soft-prefer (best-effort region with fallback), and regional-fallback tiers. 2) Persist retention profiles per-tenant and expose them in endpoint configuration. 3) Generate signed evidence bundles on-demand or via scheduled exports containing routing decisions, retention metadata, and audit manifests. 4) Keep operational overhead low by integrating with existing routing and billing traces so evidence is reconstructable without high-cost, full-request logging.

Scope (MVP): Policy DSL v1, Console create/edit flow, runtime tagging of requests with resolved region and retention profile, evidence export job producing gzipped ndjson with a signed manifest, and simple API endpoint for customers to request evidence bundles. Excludes: per-token content-level residency parsing, cross-tenant aggregated proofs, and on-prem agent for air-gapped customers (future work).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Admin can create a geo-anchor policy (strict/soft/fallback) in Console; 2) Requests to hosted endpoints include region tags and retention profile ids visible in traces; 3) Evidence export API returns a signed bundle (manifest + records) that passes signature verification with the platform signing key; 4) Retention change events are tracked and appear in the evidence for the requested window; 5) End-to-end integration tests cover policy enforcement and export pipeline; 6) Documentation and runbook published.
implementation_notes: Policy DSL: YAML-first with keys: policy_id, mode (strict|soft|fallback), allowed_regions[], fallback_sequence[]. Retention profiles: storage TTLs + delete-backoff + retention_id. Evidence bundle format: gzipped ndjson, each line a flat record with: timestamp, request_id, resolved_region, retention_id, decision_reason, route_version. Signed manifest: SHA256 digest per file, signed by platform KMS key; include certificate chain and timestamp. Runtime changes: attach policy_id & resolved_region to request context, emit compact evidence event to evidence-export topic. Export pipeline: batch from topic -> serialize -> compress -> sign -> store in customer_buckets OR provide one-time download URL.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP rollout, 2 weeks): enable policy creation read-only and evidence export for a small set of pilot tenants; Phase 2 (soft-enforce, 2 weeks): route respecting soft policies but allow fallback, collect metrics; Phase 3 (hard-enforce, 1 week): enforce strict pins with clear errors and recommended fallback policies; Phase 4: expand to larger tenant set and add scheduling + retention lifecycle automation.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Evidence bundle could leak sensitive payloads -> Mitigation: Include only metadata (no user content) in MVP and require customer KMS for bundle encryption; Risk: Runtime overhead increases latency -> Mitigation: Emit lightweight events async, do not block request; Risk: Customers request cross-region exports -> Mitigation: Add policy validations and deny unsupported combinations; Risk: Signing key compromise -> Mitigation: rotate KMS keys, provide revocation logs.
open_questions: 1) Should evidence include hashed prefixes of input to help customers correlate requests without including content?; 2) Do we need per-tenant BYOK for signing (customer-supplied signing key) or platform sign + customer KMS encrypt?; 3) SLAs for evidence export generation (SLA vs best-effort)?; 4) How granular should retention profiles be (route-level vs tenant-level)?

2025-02-24 — Ravi Shah (Infra): Confirmed async evidence pipeline acceptable; suggested Kafka retention window implications and proposed compaction policy.

notes_for_engineering:
- Emit smallest possible evidence event from runtime to avoid P95 latency impact.
- Worker groups should batch and cap bundle sizes; support incremental exports.
- Provide preview endpoint that returns bundle manifest and digest without exposing the full bundle.
- Document KMS key usage patterns and rotation steps.
ux_acceptance_criteria: - Console: create geo policy modal with clear help text for strict vs soft semantics; - Retention selector dropdown listing retained profiles with durations; - Evidence page that shows last export time, manifest digest, and download link (for authorized users); - Error states documented for strict pin violations.
qa_test_plan: - Unit tests for DSL parser and manifest signer; - Integration tests where synthetic requests exercise strict/soft/fallback behaviors; - E2E test generating evidence bundle and validating signature + manifest contents; - Regression tests to confirm no request latency regressions >5ms p95 introduced.
legal_requirements:
- Evidence bundles must include an immutable audit manifest referencing customer KMS key id when customer BYOK is enabled.
- Retention deletion logs must be retained for 395 days for jurisdictions requiring one-year proof.
- Exported evidence must be accompanied by a chain-of-custody note created by platform automation.
follow_up_tasks: Design microcopy for Residency Console; Add telemetry for soft-fail rates and policy mismatches; Create runbook for incoming compliance requests; Evaluate BYOK signing options and cost for HSM usage.
